newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures surge on stronger dollar.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures surge on stronger dollar.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures ended sharply higher on Wednesday, as the yen's losses against the dollar triggered active buying by individual investors, traders said.
May and July futures were up by the daily 500 yen limit at the close, and the benchmark January 1998 contract ended up 320 yen at 15,560 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 69,933 lots.

The stronger Chicago market overnight encouraged investors to buy, traders said. "The yen's steep losses accelerated the buying," a trader said. The dollar powered to a fresh four-year high of 123.18 yen in mid-afternoon.
The spot March contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.71-1/4 per bushel at 0755 GMT, up from $2.70-1/2 at Tuesday's close.
The spot March of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.36-1/4 at 0755 GMT, down from $7.37 at Tuesday's close.
